subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw extend `api.runtime.gateway.request` beyond bundled/trusted official plugins to ordinary external plugin-to-plugin calls, and what authorization or capability contract should gate that access?
rationale: The remaining work changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose whether external plugins may invoke arbitrary plugin-owned Gateway methods.

options.title: Design explicit capability contract
options.body: Expose external plugin-to-plugin calls only through declared capabilities or allowlisted Gateway methods with caller attribution, scope checks, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only runtime Gateway calls
options.body: Leave current main's bundled/trusted-official restriction in place and direct external plugins toward existing context, hook, or future service APIs.

options.title: Allow raw method dispatch
options.body: Expose a general method-string caller for more flexibility, accepting a larger compatibility and security surface.

recommendation.title: Design explicit capability contract
recommendation.body: Expose external plugin-to-plugin calls only through declared capabilities or allowlisted Gateway methods with caller attribution, scope checks, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current trusted-only Gateway runtime surface and is the strongest history match for the plugin/Gateway security boundary.
